title: add representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline
author: Amy Chen
description: Motivation: provide a reproducible set of representative workload runners, lightweight profiling baselines, and an automated reporting pipeline so that perf engineers and runtime owners can reliably run nightly/PR-level benchmarks and produce standardized HTML/CSV reports. This PR adds: 1) workload runners for chat/text-generation, embedding batches, and long-context streaming; 2) a small profiling baseline harness that captures memory, CPU, and per-token latency histograms; 3) a reporting pipeline that aggregates artifacts from CI, produces a per-run JSON summary and human-readable HTML report, and uploads to S3; 4) a small runner shim to make experiments deterministic (seed control, warmup/steady-state phases). Checklist: - [x] add workload runners and examples - [x] add baseline profiling harness - [x] implement reporting/export pipeline - [x] add CI job (benchmark-smoke) - [x] update README and runbook - [x] add Linear ticket references Related: ENG-1023 (benchmarking initiative), ENG-1107 (profiling baseline design). How to run locally: `python -m benchlab.runner --workload chat --model ./models/gpt-small --seq-len 512 --iters 100 --out ./out` Reporting: `python -m benchlab.report --input ./out --format html,csv --upload s3://redwood-bench-reports/nightly/2024-11-01/` Notes on reproducibility: runners include warmup and measurement windows; seed control exposed as `--seed`; environment variables documented in README. Backwards compatibility: this is additive and does not affect runtime serving code. CI artifacts: smoke runs produce sample CSV/HTML attached to the PR for reviewers. For larger nightly runs we rely on the scheduled workflow.
